To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) cortical speech perception in noise is mediated by a frontotemporal network that includes the superior temporal gyrus (STG) and the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG); (ii) this network is activated by both speech and non-speech sounds; (iii) the STG contains a hierarchy of speech-selective areas that are organized along a ventrodorsal axis, with more posterior and dorsal areas responding more strongly to non-speech sounds than to speech; and

the neural correlates of speech in noise perception are located in the left hemisphere in the primary auditory cortex (A1), in the superior temporal gyrus (STG) and in the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG).

the cortical processing of speech in noise is mediated by the interplay between the auditory and visual systems, with the visual system playing a dominant role in the processing of speech sounds in noise, and that the visual system can be modulated by auditory stimuli, and vice versa.
